title: Routes and networks: set 1
sourceNote: An original set written for this group. It is not a CAT previous-year set.
instructions: CAT marking: +3 right, -1 wrong multiple choice, 0 for a wrong type-in answer.
Type-in answers take a number only: no %, ₹ or units. Use a decimal, not a fraction.

groups.title: Six towns
groups.text:
Six towns, P, Q, R, S, T and U, are joined by two-way roads. The roads and their lengths in km are:

P-Q 4, P-R 7, Q-R 2, Q-S 6, R-S 3, R-T 8, S-T 2, S-U 9, T-U 4.

There are no other roads. A route may not pass through the same town twice.

questions.text: What is the length, in km, of the shortest route from P to U?
Which towns, in order, does the shortest route from P to U pass through?
options: P, Q, R, S, T, U

questions.text: The road R-S is closed. What is now the length, in km, of the shortest route from P to U?
How many different routes from P to S use exactly three roads?
